public_rationale: The O’Reilly survey supports the narrower observation that many respondents' companies were still experimenting. It does not measure the share of all LLM applications that were tests. Klarna demonstrates substantial production use, but cannot establish the opposite majority. The available evidence does not settle Marcus's quantitative claim.
limitations: Survey respondents are not interchangeable with projects or usage volume.
Production examples cannot establish an industry-wide proportion.
The principal pre-post survey predates the statement by several months.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most uses of LLMs so far have been for testing rather than production systems.

statement.excerpt: So far most uses of LLMs have been for testing, not production-level systems.
statement.document_title: When Will the GenAI Bubble Burst?

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion concerns enterprise adoption, so I read uses as enterprise LLM applications or projects.
Testing includes experiments, proofs of concept and pilots; production means live operational use.
So far describes activity up to March 31, 2024. No starting date is supplied, so the start remains unspecified.
Respondent counts, organization counts, project counts and request volumes are different denominators and cannot be substituted without justification.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence establishes that more than half of enterprise LLM applications attempted by the post date were testing rather than production systems.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence with the same denominator establishes that half or fewer were testing.
